players.product: SATA and PCIe 3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0 NVMe SSD controller chips (consumer, industrial and enterprise; enterprise PCIe 5.0 in mass-production testing) and UFS 3.1 embedded storage controllers

quarterly_data.quarter: Maxio Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (04-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director and general manager Li Guoyang (2025 annual results briefing): end-2025 inventory rose because high-end products are a larger share of the mix (higher unit value), production scheduling cycles for some high-end products lengthened so it raised stock in line with delivery cycles, and it stocked ahead to secure supply amid international trade protectionism; in 2026 it will track supply and demand and adjust its inventory strategy dynamically.

quarterly_data.quarter: Maxio Technology results briefing Q&A: 2025 annual (04-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Director and general manager Li Guoyang (2025 annual results briefing): storage module makers' 2025 profit surge came from DRAM and NAND flash price spikes, a cyclical gain, while controller makers are not directly affected by NAND prices and are driven by technology iterations (PCIe 4.0/5.0, UFS upgrades), so its upside from price cycles is smaller but earnings are steadier. The company said its consumer PCIe Gen5 SSD controller is in scaled volume shipment, the enterprise PCIe Gen5 SSD controller is in mass-production testing and the UFS 3.1 controller is in mass production, expected to contribute revenue from 2026; chairman Fang Xiaoling said development and tape-out of next-generation PCIe Gen6/Gen7 and UFS 5.0 chips will proceed on plan.
